design_rationale: Five school classes were randomly assigned as clusters to three conditions (convivial eating, positive restriction + convivial eating, and control) with the constraint that adjacent visible classrooms received the same condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was done at the cluster (classroom) level with only five clusters under non-random constraints (adjacent classrooms matched), sequence generation/concealment details are not provided, and clustering was not accounted for in assignment or baseline comparability.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The eligible school expected five school classes with each 20–25 children during the study period. Since individual randomisation is not possible in a classroom-based study, two school classes were assigned to the CE condition, two to the PR + CE condition and one class to the control condition. Assignment was random on condition that school classes that could see each other physically (through large windows between class rooms) were in the same experimental condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and teachers could not be blinded to the intervention, and a per-protocol complete-case analysis was performed excluding children who missed sessions S1 or S8 rather than a true intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Children who missed S1 or S8 were excluded from the dataset. Children from both intervention conditions (CE and PR + CE) attended on average 7.8 ± 0.6 of the eight convivial eating sessions, ensuring sufficient presence to be included in the dataset. The final dataset included 99 children.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 99 of 102 consented children (97%) post-intervention and 93 children (91%) at the 9-month follow-up, representing very low and balanced attrition across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Hundred and two parents out of 112 (91%) signed the informed consent... The final dataset included 99 children... A longer-term follow-up was executed at nine months (N = 93)... CE n = 35; PR + CE n = 40; Control n = 18.

domain_judgments.rationale: Vegetable intake was measured objectively by weighing containers before and after consumption with high-precision scales using identical standardized procedures across all conditions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Vegetable intake was assessed per child during each session. Intake was calculated by subtracting the leftover weight from the weight before consumption, using a Kern & Sohn EMB600-1 weighing scales, with a precision of 0.1 g.

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial pre-registration or pre-specified statistical analysis plan was cited, and multiple exploratory post-hoc subgroup and non-parametric tests were performed across several endpoints.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The data were analysed using IBM SPSS Statistics 19.0, with a significance level of p < 0.05... Kruskal-Wallis tests with subsequent Mann-Whitney tests were used to investigate differences in carrot intake between conditions. In addition, for each condition separately, carrot intake changes between S1 and S8, or between S1 and the follow-up session, were analysed with a Wilcoxon Signed Ranks test.

overall_summary: The study has some concerns overall primarily due to cluster-level allocation across only five classrooms with visibility constraints and lack of allocation concealment, per-protocol exclusion of participants missing sessions, and absence of a pre-registered statistical analysis plan.

design_rationale: Four childcare centres were recruited and two were randomly assigned to the intervention condition, representing a cluster-randomized design.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 4 childcare centres were randomized (2 to intervention, 2 to control) with no details provided on sequence generation or allocation concealment, and a significant baseline difference in pumpkin intake was observed between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two childcare locations served as intervention group (N 125) and two locations formed the control group (N 125)... Two childcare centres were randomly assigned to the intervention condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: Interventions were delivered as intended within normal daycare routines by staff who were unaware of the full comparative design until after the study, and appropriate mixed-effects models accounting for clustering/repeated measures were used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After the study had finished, parents and day care employees were informed about the exact study design explaining both the intervention and control condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: A substantial proportion of children were excluded from analyses per vegetable (e.g., around 180-213 analyzed out of 250 enrolled) due to requiring at least two measurements at both pre- and post-test, with no analysis comparing missingness between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: children needed to have at least two intake measurements for a vegetable at pre- and post-test to be included in the data analyses for that vegetable.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome of vegetable intake was assessed objectively via precise pre- and post-weighing of vegetable portions out of the children's view by the research team.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: During the pre- and post-test, the research team weighed the vegetable cups before (mean 109 ± 6.8 g; range 84e137 g) and after consumption, out of the children's view. Vegetable intake was calculated by subtracting the leftovers from the pre-weight.

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration number or pre-specified statistical analysis plan is mentioned, leaving open the possibility of selective reporting of analyses across multiple vegetable preparations and testing behaviors.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A mixed model analysis was done with vegetable intake as dependent variable, and time (2 levels), condition (2 levels) and the interaction time*condition as fixed factors and subject as random factor.

overall_summary: The study has some concerns overall due to a very small number of randomized clusters (four centres) without reported allocation concealment methods, notable exclusions from post-test intake analyses without verification of missing-at-random status, and lack of pre-registration.

design_rationale: Participants (173 families) were randomly assigned to one of three conditions using blocked randomization with allocation concealed in opaque envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was randomized using blocks and concealed until after baseline assessments using opaque envelopes, with no baseline differences between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The 173 participants who agreed to be visited were randomly allocated to 1 of the 3 conditions by using blocked randomization; for every block of 30 participants, 10 were allocated to each condition. ... Before a home visit, researchers carried with them an opaque envelope containing a slip of paper on which was written 1 of the 3 conditions. At the child's home and after the baseline assessments, the researcher opened the envelope out of sight of the participants.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and researchers could not be blinded to the behavioral intervention, and 9 participants were excluded from the analysis specifically for protocol deviations (failure to follow intervention procedures), precluding a strict intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Seven children were excluded from the analyses because they were ill during the intervention period and 9 children because parents told us that they had failed to follow the intervention procedures (eg, changed target vegetable, changed the reward). The sample available for analysis of the intervention phase, therefore, was 149.

domain_judgments.rationale: Attrition was relatively low (81% completed across all time points, 86% post-intervention), balanced across groups (47 in TR, 46 in SR, 47 in Control), and reasons for dropouts/exclusions were documented and unlikely to depend on the true outcome values.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 173 participants who completed baseline assessments, 8 families withdrew because of difficulty scheduling subsequent sessions. Seven children were excluded from the analyses because they were ill during the intervention period and 9 children because parents told us that they had failed to follow the intervention procedures (eg, changed target vegetable, changed the reward). The sample available for analysis of the intervention phase, therefore, was 149. There were also 9 missing outcomes from the follow-up assessments; therefore, the longitudinal multivariate analyses across all time points had a sample size of 140.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors were unblinded to condition and administered the behavioral intake and liking tests in the child's home, which could have subtly influenced the child's behavior and responses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Although the researchers were blinded to group allocation during baseline assessments, they were unblinded thereafter because they had to teach parents the feeding techniques. As a result, they may have inadvertently given greater encouragement to intervention participants than to control subjects. However, the children's intake of their target vegetable was measured objectively.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered prospectively (ISRCTN42922680) and all prespecified primary outcomes across all time points are fully reported according to a clear analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcomes were liking and intake of the target vegetable, which were assessed at baseline, immediately after the intervention, and 1 and 3 mo later. ... This trial is registered as ISRCTN42922680.

overall_summary: The study was well-conducted with proper random sequence generation and allocation concealment, but some concerns arise due to unblinded outcome assessment during home visits and the exclusion of participants who did not adhere to the protocol rather than analyzing all randomized participants by intention-to-treat.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized controlled trial in which mothers/infants were randomized to either the intervention group or the control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: The authors state that participants were randomised, but do not provide any details regarding sequence generation or allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Mothers were randomised to either the intervention (n = 20) or control group (n = 20) after they had consented to the study and before they had completed any questionnaires.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although mothers were not blinded due to the nature of feeding interventions at home, protocol deviations were minimal, standard feeding instructions were followed, and analysis assessed the effect of assignment without problematic post-randomization exclusions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Mothers were randomised to either the intervention (n = 20) or control group (n = 20)... Both groups were asked not to introduce any other new foods or flavours to the infants during the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Attrition was low (4/40, 10%), balanced between groups, reasons were clearly documented, and unlikely to be related to the outcome for the primary post-intervention assessments.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the original 40 mother–infant dyads who agreed to take part in the study, complete data were obtained from 36 mothers (18 in each group). Reasons for non-completion included missed appointments (n = 2), relocation (n = 1) and return to work (n = 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Intake was measured objectively by weighing, but cessation of feeding depended on judging infant refusal cues, and for liking ratings the researchers were explicitly unblinded, which the authors acknowledge may have affected ratings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Vegetable intake recorded on Days 25, 26, 33 and 34... remaining vegetable on the infant’s face, hands and on the chair was collected and returned to the bowl. The remaining puree was re-weighed... However, researchers were not blind to the group assignment and this may have affected judgements.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no mention of a pre-registered trial protocol or analysis plan, and some post hoc decisions regarding outlier exclusion based on boxplots were applied.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Where data were outliers as detected by boxplots, these were removed and where infants were unwell on the day of testing, their data were excluded... SPSS (v20, Chicago, USA) was used for all statistical analyses...

overall_summary: The study is judged to have some concerns overall due to insufficient reporting of sequence generation and allocation concealment methods, unblinded assessors for subjective liking outcomes, and lack of a pre-registered statistical analysis protocol.

design_rationale: Participants' families were randomly assigned to one of three experimental groups (fruit book, vegetable book, or control).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although random assignment is stated and baseline characteristics were comparable across groups, the method of sequence generation and allocation concealment was not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Families were randomly assigned to one of three experimental groups: a ‘fruit book’ group (n = 42...); a ‘vegetable book’ group (n = 46...); or a control group (n = 39...).

domain_judgments.rationale: Given the nature of the behavioral shared-reading intervention, blinding was impossible, but parents adhered closely to the taste exposure protocol across all conditions without significant unintended deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Parents were also, necessarily, the agents of the intervention – they shared the books with their children and provided repeated taste exposures to the target foods afterwards – so they could not be blind to experimental condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: There was substantial attrition from baseline (n=127) to post-intervention (n=105, 17% missing) and 3-month follow-up (n=78, ~39% missing), and analyses were complete-case rather than intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 127 parents who returned questionnaires at baseline, 105 completed the visual familiarization and taste-exposure phases of the intervention and returned the questionnaires sent out immediately post-intervention... Seventy-eight parents returned follow-up questionnaires three months later... The distribution of the 28 families who dropped out between postintervention and follow-up again did not differ from chance

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessment relied on subjective parent reports of child liking and food consumption, and parents were fully aware of intervention group assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In contrast to previous similar work, measures were obtained through parent-report questionnaires completed at home rather than experimenter ratings collected in a laboratory... Involving parents in these ways, while crucial to our objectives, opens the window for social desirability biases in the reporting of children’s liking and consumption of the target foods

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial pre-registration or prospective statistical analysis plan is referenced, leaving potential for selection among multiple reported timepoints, foods, and questionnaire subscales.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary experimental hypotheses, that children would show greater increases in liking and consumption of foods to which they had received prior visual familiarization, were tested using mixed ANOVA.

overall_summary: The study has high overall risk of bias due to the reliance on unblinded subjective parent reports for the primary outcomes (liking and intake), compounded by missing data at follow-up and lack of a pre-registered analysis plan.

design_rationale: The authors explicitly report that schools were randomly assigned to conditions in a randomized controlled trial design ('Preschool A was randomly assigned to the intervention first condition and Preschool B to the control/delayed intervention condition').

domain_judgments.rationale: With only two preschool clusters randomized (one per condition), random allocation cannot ensure balance, sequence generation and allocation concealment details are not described, and substantial baseline differences in vegetable consumption existed between the groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Preschool A was randomly assigned to the intervention first condition and Preschool B to the control/delayed intervention condition. ... At baseline, average vegetable consumption was 10.7 g (standard deviation [SD] 8.5 g) at Preschool A and 6.2 g (SD 6 g) at Preschool B.

domain_judgments.rationale: Teachers and preschool staff were aware of condition assignment, and although the intervention protocol was generally adhered to in the preschool setting, potential school-level deviations or context differences could arise without blinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Teachers were instructed not to exert any pressure on the children to eat the vegetables; however, they were encouraged to discuss what they were eating, as is their normal practice (eg, 'These peppers are green.').

domain_judgments.rationale: Data were available for nearly all consented children (88 to 94 out of 96 across primary ANOVA and regression models), with very low levels of missing outcome data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Data from 96 children were analyzed. ... The mixed factorial analysis of variance produced a significant time-condition interaction on consumption averaged across all three vegetables ... F(1,88)=10.81

domain_judgments.rationale: Vegetable consumption was measured objectively by weighing pre-portioned bags and leftovers to the nearest gram, an objective method unlikely to be influenced by lack of assessor blinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All bags were weighed to the nearest gram and labeled. ... At the end of the lunch period, the teachers instructed students to put any waste back into the bags. Researchers picked up the bags later from the schools, weighed them, and calculated intake to the nearest gram.

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-registration or published trial protocol is cited, leaving some concern regarding potential flexibility in analysis choices and reporting of post-hoc vegetable-specific comparisons.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A 2 (time) 2 (condition) mixed factorial analysis of variance was used to test whether vegetable consumption increased over time in the intervention group vs the control group. ... Follow-up analyses of variance were run for each vegetable separately.

overall_summary: The study is at high overall risk of bias primarily due to allocating only two clusters (one school per arm) without allocation concealment details and with large baseline differences between schools, in addition to some concerns regarding lack of pre-registration.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to the control or treatment group using a computer random number generator (www.random.org).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although a random number generator was used to generate the allocation sequence, no details are provided regarding allocation concealment prior to assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Children were randomized to control (n 12) or treatment groups (n 12) using a random number generator (www.random.org). Families and researchers were not blinded to the conditions.

domain_judgments.rationale: Given the nature of the behavioral intervention, participants and parents could not be blinded, but compliance was tracked via daily checklists and home visits, the intervention protocol was adhered to, and all randomized participants were analyzed in their assigned groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Families and researchers were not blinded to the conditions. ... In both the control and treatment groups, parents were given specific instructions on when and how to present snacks to children.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 24 randomized children completed all study visits, resulting in complete outcome data with zero attrition.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Twenty-four children participated in the study and all completed five out of five visits, for a retention rate of 100%.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcomes of vegetable and granola bar intake were measured objectively via pre- and post-weighing of food containers, making measurement bias unlikely despite lack of blinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Intake was measured as the difference between pre- and post-weights of the foods provided. In post-weighing, it was not possible to completely separate leftover ranch dressing from the vegetables...

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-registration or published statistical analysis plan was mentioned to rule out selective reporting among potential analyses and multiple exploratory comparisons.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: General Linear Model repeated measures analysis of variance was conducted to compare vegetable and granola bar intake between control and treatment groups across the 4-week study. Both within- and between-subjects models were tested.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is rated as 'some concerns' due to the absence of reported allocation concealment procedures in Domain 1 and the lack of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified analysis plan in Domain 5.

design_rationale: The study is a cluster randomized controlled trial in which 11 preschools were randomly allocated to one of four conditions using an online random list generator.

domain_judgments.rationale: Preschool clusters were stratified by size and randomly allocated using a computer random list generator with allocation concealed until after recruitment and consent was complete.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: One preschool in each stratum was assigned to each intervention condition using an online list generator (https://www.random.org/lists)... Preschool managers were not informed of their condition allocation until all preschools were recruited (after consent) and randomized.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding of preschool staff was not possible, there were protocol non-compliances, and the primary analysis excluded participants who did not complete assessments or adhere to exposures rather than following an intention-to-treat approach.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Preschools varied in the extent to which they delivered the two components of the NE program... some preschools did not comply with the repeated taste exposure protocol because the staff continued to offer the usual snack immediately after the vegetable snack. In addition, intake data were excluded from analyses where children in the TE conditions had fewer than five taste exposures (n = 3)... Children in the NE and control condition with missing intake data... were excluded from the main analysis (n = 75).

domain_judgments.rationale: There was substantial attrition (36% missing data overall, reducing the sample from 219 to 140) with differential retention across arms, particularly affecting the control condition (only 16 children remaining from 34 enrolled), and complete-case analysis was used without imputation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In all, 219 children were enrolled in the study... Included in the final analysis were 140 children (70 boys and 70 girls) with complete intake assessments at all four time points... there was a high rate of missing data over time for the complete set of intake data, including follow-ups (36%). As a result of this, there was a substantially smaller sample size in the control condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: Vegetable intake was measured objectively by weighing pre- and post-consumption snack portions using digital scales, minimizing risk of assessor measurement bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Each vegetable portion was weighed (to the nearest 0.01 g) before and after each snack time using a digital scale (Mettler PJ4000; Mettler-Toledo LLC) by the research team. Fresh mooli was peeled and cut into bite-size pieces... Snack bags were collected after the exposures and were reweighed immediately to calculate intake.

domain_judgments.rationale: While the trial was preregistered on ClinicalTrials.gov, the specific statistical analytic approach (dichotomizing into eaters vs noneaters and restricting amount analysis only to baseline eaters) was post-hoc/adapted due to skewed distribution, raising some concerns for selection of the reported result.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Intake data for all time points resulted in a positive skew as many children ate 0 g mooli. Therefore, a complex samples logistic regression analysis was conducted to examine what factor predicted children eating at least some of the mooli (classed as eaters). Next a complex samples general linear repeated measures analysis of variance was performed to examine the predictors of the amount consumed, when children had eaten some of the mooli.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high due to substantial missing outcome data (36% loss overall with marked differential loss leading to an underrepresented control group) and non-adherence/per-protocol exclusions rather than an intention-to-treat analysis in deviations from intended interventions.

design_rationale: The authors describe the experiments as randomized: participants in the crossover test-meal studies were randomized to condition order, and in the pilot intervention trial, children were randomly assigned to intervention or control groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although random assignment is stated and baseline characteristics were reported as similar, details of sequence generation and allocation concealment are completely absent.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Prior to the first visit, children were randomly assigned to the intervention (n=7) or control groups (n=9). Baseline measures (sex, ethnic breakdown, BMI z-score, and age) were similar across the two groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Due to the nature of the packaging/branding intervention, participants and researchers were aware of the assigned intervention, introducing potential performance bias or subtle deviations in home-delivery execution.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Although the researchers were not blinded to who was receiving the treatment, the nutrition education lessons were run in small groups of two to three children in each, made up of children who were from both experimental groups. Thus, both groups received the same nutrition counseling.

domain_judgments.rationale: Three of 19 recruited participants (15.8%) dropped out due to scheduling conflicts and were excluded from analysis with no intention-to-treat or sensitivity analyses reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 19 children were recruited, but due to scheduling conflicts, only 16 families finished all seven visits and the findings from these families will be described herein.

domain_judgments.rationale: Leftover containers were brought back and weighed by researchers who were unblinded to group assignment, and consumption could also be affected by parental compliance and reporting at home.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In addition, parents were responsible for bringing leftover F&V back to the lab the following week so they could be post-weighed.

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration or pre-specified statistical analysis plan was mentioned for these pilot studies, allowing potential flexibility in selecting reported outcomes and analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All Stroop sessions were recorded using a hand-held audio recording device... Higher scores on both the color and Food Brand Stroop suggested greater cognitive interference.

overall_summary: Across all domains there are some concerns due to lack of reporting on sequence generation and allocation concealment, unblinded participants and researchers, exclusion of post-randomization dropouts, and absence of a pre-registered analysis protocol. Consequently, the overall risk-of-bias judgment is some concerns.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that allocation to the exposure or control group was randomly assigned at the daycare center unit level ('어린이집 단위로 무선 배정되었다').

domain_judgments.rationale: Although cluster randomization at the daycare center level was reported, no details are provided regarding the sequence generation method or allocation concealment, and only 4 centers were randomized.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 노출집단과 통제집단 중 어떤 집단에 아동이 참여하는가는 어린이집 단위로 무선 배정되었다(노출 24명, 51.1%; 통제 23명, 48.9%).

domain_judgments.rationale: The intervention was delivered per protocol by trained teachers with fidelity monitoring (85-100% adherence), and participants in daycare centers received the intended program without evidence of unintended deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 통제 집단의 경우 사전, 사후 측정은 노출집단과 동일하게 이루어졌으나 실험조건에서 6개월 동안 노출프로그램을 진행하는 동안 프로그램이 진행되지 않은 채 기존의 보육활동이 진행되었다.

domain_judgments.rationale: Post-randomization exclusions occurred (e.g. 7 children who already consumed >90% of vegetables at baseline and 4 absent children), and several children had missing measurement sessions filled by single-day data, raising some concerns.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 부모가 동의한 54명의 아동 중, 프로그램 전 이미 채소의 90%이상 섭취한 7명의 아동은 노출프로그램의 효과성을 알아보기 위한 본 연구의 목적을 고려할 때 연구대상으로 적합하지 않다고 판단하고 분석에서 제외하여 총 47명... 최종분석에 포함되었다.

domain_judgments.rationale: Vegetable consumption was objectively measured and recorded via standardized observation and videotaping with high inter-rater reliability, making assessment bias unlikely despite lack of explicit blinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 측정의 신뢰도를 위해 한 아동 당 한 명의 연구자와 두 명의 관찰자가 섭취량을 측정하였다. 본 연구의 관찰자간 신뢰도는 96.7%～100%였다.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no mention of a pre-registered trial protocol or statistical analysis plan, and specific nutrients were selected post hoc for reporting from a wider set of nutritional data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 마지막으로, 노출 프로그램이 실제 식사 행동도 변화시켜 전반적인 영양 개선에까지 영향을 미쳤는지 확인하기 위해 우선 CAN-Pro 4.0을 이용해 분석한 아동이 섭취한 많은 영양소 중에서, 본 연구의 목적에 맞게 채소 섭취와 관련되는 영양소를 기존의 연구들...을 참조하여 선별하였다.

overall_summary: The study is judged to have some concerns overall due to insufficient details on sequence generation/allocation concealment in a 4-cluster randomized design (Domain 1), post-randomization participant exclusions (Domain 3), and lack of a pre-registered analysis plan with selective reporting of specific nutrients (Domain 5).

design_rationale: The authors describe the study as a 'randomized, controlled, parallel-group study' where participants were randomly assigned to either the veg-only or control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants were randomly assigned, the specific method of sequence generation and allocation concealment mechanism are not detailed in the paper text (referring to a published protocol).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At the start of CF (4–6 mo), infants were randomly assigned to either veg-only or control groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants/parents were effectively blinded to group assignment by coding and color-labeling foods, and the intervention was delivered as intended with minimal deviations and high compliance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Throughout this study, parents were unaware as to which group they had been originally assigned (because foods were named for their color not their content).

domain_judgments.rationale: There was differential completion/missingness between groups (veg-only 84% vs control 70% completed target vegetable intake), and authors noted non-completers differed systematically from completers, indicating missingness may not be completely at random.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of these, 92% (veg-only, 84%; control, 70%) completed by providing intake data (grams) for the target vegetables (broccoli and spinach) for the primary analysis at 9 mo of age. Loss to follow-up was due to family time constraints (n 8), and 1 infant was excluded from all analyses as they had started consuming PediaSure (Abbott Nutrition) due to feeding issues.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome of intake was objectively weighed using digital scales, mothers were blinded to assignment codes, and video coders for behavioral outcomes were blinded independent raters with high inter-rater reliability.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Mothers measured and recorded intake of the study foods only during the first and last 4 d of the 4-wk intervention and then for each target food at 9 mo using provided digital scales ( 1 g). ... To assess rate of acceptance, an independent research assistant who was blinded to the originally assigned groups was trained to score the videos according to a set of coding rules

domain_judgments.rationale: A detailed study protocol was published in advance, and reported primary and secondary outcomes correspond with the pre-specified protocol plan and standard mixed-effects models.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A detailed protocol has been published (29). The primary outcome was intake (grams) of target vegetables (broccoli and spinach) at 9 mo of age.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as 'some concerns' due to lack of explicit detail regarding sequence generation and allocation concealment in the main manuscript text, as well as differential attrition between intervention groups with evidence that missingness was not completely at random.

design_rationale: The study is explicitly described as a 4-arm randomized controlled trial evaluating interventions against an attention control condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the trial is randomized and baseline characteristics were comparable across groups, specific details of sequence generation and allocation concealment are referred to a separate protocol paper and not detailed in the text.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Information regarding, for example, recruitment of participants and randomization can be found in the study protocol, as well as in the flow chart depicted in Supplemental Figure 1 (21).

domain_judgments.rationale: The behavioral nature of the intervention meant blinding of participants was not possible, but an intention-to-treat approach was used via linear mixed models without evidence of protocol deviations affecting trial outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Because LMM analysis facilitates an intention-to-treat analysis, all participants with data for 1 one time point (t0, t18, or t24) were included in the analyses.

domain_judgments.rationale: Linear mixed models utilized all available data, dropouts were balanced and not related to intervention group, and retention across follow-up points was relatively high.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Dropping out was not related to maternal BMI, maternal age, maternal vegetable intake, intervention group, or household income.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcomes were assessed using standardized, objective methods (weighed dietary recalls, objective task measurement, blinded video coding of feeding behavior, and standardized anthropometry).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The coders were not familiar with the families in the videos they were allocated, nor aware of these families’ group status (experimental compared with control).

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is rated as some concerns primarily due to the lack of explicit description within the text of the random sequence generation and allocation concealment methods, despite prospective registration and appropriate objective outcome measurements and intention-to-treat analyses.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to either the intervention or control group using a permuted-block schedule generated by an external statistician.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization sequence was generated by an external statistician using permuted blocks, allocation was concealed after baseline assessment, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After baseline assessment, participants were randomly allocated to an intervention or a control group by an external statistician. A permutated-block schedule with blocks of 4 within each assessment clinic location was used to optimize the balance of participant socioeconomic characteristics across the groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were analyzed according to their allocated groups using an intention-to-treat framework, and interventions were delivered in standard practice settings with facilitator supervision to ensure fidelity.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An intention-to-treat approach to analysis was used as far as missing data permitted (no imputations were made)... Attendance at ≥2 sessions for module 1 was n = 229 (65%) and module 2 was n = 130 (45% of those retained at module commencement).

domain_judgments.rationale: There was differential attrition between groups (26% in the intervention vs. 19% in the control group, P = .01) without imputation or sensitivity analysis to account for missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At follow-up (20 months from baseline), total attrition was 22% (n = 157)... Withdrawal was higher among younger and less educated mothers (all, P < .001) (Table 3) and in the intervention group (26%, n = 92) than in the control group (19%, n = 65; P = .01), but it did not differ according to mothers’ BMI (P = .51). However, there were no differences by group in the baseline characteristics of those who withdrew (data not shown).

domain_judgments.rationale: While anthropometric outcome assessors were blinded, primary behavioral feeding outcomes relied entirely on self-reports by mothers who were aware of their intervention group assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Anthropometric measurements were taken by trained study staff blinded to participant group and independent of intervention delivery... Maternal feeding practices were self-reported by using validated questionnaires and study-developed items.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial and its protocol were registered prospectively with pre-specified outcome measures, and results are reported consistent with the planned protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trial has been registered in the Australian and New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ACTRN 12608000056392)... The protocol has been published elsewhere.7,16

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged to have some concerns due to differential attrition between study arms (26% intervention vs 19% control) without imputation, and reliance on unblinded maternal self-report for key feeding practice outcomes.

design_rationale: The study is described as an individually randomised, parallel-group trial where participants were randomly assigned to intervention or control groups using a block randomisation matrix generated by an independent statistician.

domain_judgments.rationale: An independent statistician generated the block randomisation matrix, balancing on feeding method, and baseline characteristics appear well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An independent statistician at University College London generated a block randomisation matrix that was used in all three countries. Individual participants were randomly assigned to an intervention or control ('usual care') condition following an initial interview to establish the feeding method.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although blinding of parents and researchers was not possible due to the nature of the behavioural advice intervention, participants were unaware of the alternative arm and there were no unintended deviations that would compromise the trial.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Because of the nature of the intervention, parents in the intervention arm and researchers delivering the intervention were not blind. However, parents were unaware of the randomised controlled design and therefore neither the control nor the intervention group knew of the existence of the other.

domain_judgments.rationale: Out of 146 randomised participants, 139 completed the primary outcome taste test (minimal loss to follow-up of under 5%, balanced across groups).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In total, 139 families completed the trial, including the taste tests 1 month post-intervention (fifty-three, thirty-one and fifty-five families in the UK, Greece and Portugal, respectively).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors (both mothers and researchers) were aware of the intervention allocation, and while food intake was weighed objectively, feeding cessation criteria and subjective ratings of liking could potentially be influenced by knowledge of the assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The researcher present at the taste test was the same individual who delivered the intervention and was not therefore able to be blinded to condition. ... On completion of the test, all spilled food was returned to the bowl/jar, which was weighed again to calculate the weight of food consumed... Immediately after each feeding session, the mother and researcher separately and independently rated the infant’s apparent liking for the food on a 9-point scale

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (ISRCTN85048101) and reported prespecified primary and secondary outcomes and analyses according to plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Primary analyses were conducted for the full sample with secondary analyses conducted separately by country. ... In the UK, this trial is registered as ISRCTN85048101.

overall_summary: The study is at some concerns for overall risk of bias due to lack of blinding among the outcome assessors (both researchers and mothers) during the taste test and liking assessments, while other domains demonstrated low risk of bias.

design_rationale: The study is explicitly described as a cluster-randomized trial in which 16 school classes across eight schools were randomly assigned to one of four conditions across four waves.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although cluster randomization was employed and baseline characteristics did not differ across groups, the method of sequence generation and allocation concealment was not detailed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was scheduled in four waves, with one class randomized to each condition per wave. The numbers randomized were: ETR: n=99; EP: n=106; EA: n= 105, and C: n= 112.

domain_judgments.rationale: The intervention was delivered directly by researchers per protocol in schools, multilevel models adjusted for clustering and exposures, and no major deviations or contamination across classes were evident.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Children randomized to the intervention conditions were seen individually from Days 3 to 14, and offered a small piece of their target vegetable... Control group children had no further contacts until post-intervention assessments.

domain_judgments.rationale: Intake outcome data were available for all analyzed participants (N=422) and missingness for liking (due to school absences) was balanced across groups and unrelated to the outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Intake data were analyzed on the full sample (N=422), but liking analyses were restricted to cases with complete data (n=344) because multinomial models cannot handle missing data. There were no significant group differences in the numbers of children included at each measurement time...

domain_judgments.rationale: Intake was measured objectively by weighing bowls on digital scales, and liking was measured using an established child-friendly 3-point rating scale uniformly across all conditions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: intake (g) assessed by weighing the dish before and after using digital scales (Mettler Toledo, Switzerland)... and introduced to the 3-point ‘faces’ scale, to indicate ‘yummy’, ‘just ok’ and ‘yucky’ (Birch, Zimmerman, & Hind, 1980).

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration or pre-specified analysis plan was reported, leaving some potential for selection among reported models and sub-analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Because we had hypotheses for acquisition and maintenance, overall effects across the study period are reported first, followed by separate results for acquisition (pre- to post-intervention) and maintenance (post-intervention to follow-up).

overall_summary: The study is judged to have some concerns overall due to insufficient reporting of sequence generation and allocation concealment details, as well as the absence of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified statistical analysis plan.
